column1: # confusions.tsv -- known confusion pairs, their disambiguating context, and
# how much that context is worth.
# This and `bigram_priors.tsv` are the two files where prior knowledge is the
# deliverable rather than a means to one (ARCHITECTURE.md section 2). The
# evidence that a pair belongs here is in `confusion_candidates.tsv`, which is
# measured; what is authored here is the TEST that separates the pair and the
# WEIGHT that test carries.
# THE ZERO-SUM RULE, which is what keeps this table safe
# Every row favours one member of a pair over the other by `adjust` log2
# units, and the compiler splits it evenly: `+adjust/2` to the favoured class
# and `-adjust/2` to the other, in that context only. So a confusion rule can
# make a class more likely THAN ITS RIVAL in a named context, and can never
# make a class more likely in general. That matters because a one-sided prior
# is indistinguishable from a bias, and a bias in this table would be
# invisible in every test that looks at the pair.
# Nothing here is ever a hard rule. The adjustment is added to a score the
# matcher already produced, so a confident match outvotes it -- which is the
# behaviour rule 6 demands of the lexicon and which applies identically here.
# COLUMNS
#   a, b      the two glyphs, as literal characters
#   context   when the test applies (see below)
#   favour    `a` or `b` -- which member the context argues for
#   adjust    log2 units, split evenly between the two. AUTHORED GUESSES,
#             all of them, on chunk 8's tuning list. 1.0 means "about twice as
#             likely as the other, in this context"; the ORDER is the claim,
#             not the magnitude.
#   note      what the test actually is, in one line
# CONTEXTS the decoder can evaluate
#   digit_neighbour   the adjacent character on either side reads as a digit
#   letter_neighbour  the adjacent character on either side reads as a letter
#   upper_run         the preceding character reads as an uppercase letter
#   word_start        this is the first character of the word
#   word_end          this is the last character of the word
#   identifier        the word is identifier-shaped: enough digits, by
#                     `decode.identifier_digit_fraction`, that the lexicon
#                     term is suppressed inside it
#   lexicon_word      the path so far is still a live prefix in the lexicon
#a
